subject: chemistry
title: Layers of the Earth
welcome_lead: Peel back the planet to find its hidden layers, from rocky crust to molten core.
meta_desc: Explore Earth's structure in this KS3 chemistry adventure on the layers of the planet.
final_note: You can now picture Earth in cross-section, layer by layer.

concepts.def: Thin rocky outer layer where we live.
Thick layer of mostly solid rock that can flow slowly.
Liquid layer of iron and nickel.
Solid ball of iron and nickel at Earth's centre.
The layer of gases surrounding Earth.
Large pieces of crust that slowly move.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Earth has four main layers: crust, mantle, outer core and inner core.

The crust is the thinnest (about 5–70 km thick). The mantle is the thickest at about 2900 km.

The outer core is liquid iron and nickel. The inner core is solid iron and nickel, even though it is hotter — the huge pressure stops it from melting.

Hot enough to melt steel.
The crust is cracked into giant tectonic plates that slowly drift on the mantle. When they grind against each other we get earthquakes and volcanoes.

mcqs.q: What does an increase in entropy of a system correspond to?
options: An increase in the number of ways energy and particles can be arranged — typically a more dispersed/'disordered' state.
Entropy is just a measure of how messy a system looks visually.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.

mcqs.q: When you reverse a reaction in a Hess cycle, what happens to ΔH?
options: Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
ΔH stays the same because it's the same reaction.
ΔH becomes zero because the change cancels out.
Its sign reverses — if the forward reaction is +100 kJ/mol, the reverse is -100 kJ/mol.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
